generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, working with the whole cycle might start with a research-methods module built around hands-on data analysis, not lectures. You read its criteria to see that they reward sound method and clear interpretation, then aim your lab report there. When the feedback says your interpretation is thin, you carry that into the next report.
generatedProse.worked-example: A psychology student has a statistics assignment returned with the comment that she describes results but does not interpret them. One option is to note the mark and move on. Instead she looks back at the criteria, sees that interpretation is what the top band rewards, and plans to explain what each result means next time. Her next report reads the whole cycle, and her interpretation improves.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, the design, the criteria and the feedback on a module all point at the same skills, such as sound method and clear interpretation. Read them together and each piece of coursework can aim at the same target. The connected habit is what lifts your marks across the course.

check.body: A student reads how a module is designed, checks the marking criteria before writing, and uses the feedback on each essay to plan the next. Over the term her work improves. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That working with the whole cycle pays off: reading the design, the criteria and the feedback together kept each piece aimed at the same outcomes.
_items.feedback: Yes. She treated the three parts as one connected cycle, and each piece built on the last.

_items.text: That only the marking criteria matter, and the rest can be ignored.
_items.feedback: She used all three parts, not the criteria alone. Together they kept her work on target.

_items.text: That her tutor marked the later essays more generously.
_items.feedback: The point is not the marking. Her work improved because she worked with the whole cycle.

_items.text: That feedback is useful only at the end of a module.
_items.feedback: She used feedback after each essay, to shape the next. That is the cycle turning.
